newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi television says U.S. strikes targets.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi television says U.S. strikes targets.

text.p: An Iraqi television channel run by President Saddam Hussein's son Uday confirmed on Tuesday U.S. military strikes against targets in Iraq.

"We call the attention of citizens that we are ready to receive calls from them to express their reaction on the latest, vicious American aggression against Iraq," Shabab television said in the first official word on an American attack.
Earlier anti-aircraft fire was launched from positions in Baghdad, witnesses said, but it was not immediately clear what the fire was aimed at.
The United States said it had launched a cruise missile strike on Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi attacks in its Kurdish north.
British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said no British planes were involved in the U.S. air raids on what he said were purely military targets in rural areas.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
